quest.title: Vanquishing Phantoms
quest.description: "Now, as we face the perils of the long night..."
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x325, Primogem x60, Mora x22000, Guide to Justice x5, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x5

talks.objective: Go to the church in the capital

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Finally, you arrive at the chu{RUBY#[D]Basement}rch Florian described.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: As you approach, an ominous aura surrounds you. You get the sense that your enemy is close at hand.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (How strange... This uneasy feeling seems so real. How did they manage that?)

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Now... it is time for the final battle.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Florian, wait.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I think you should wait outside. You've already been corrupted by the Devorator once. It could easily re-enter your mind and take control of your body.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I don't think it's a good idea for you to be this close. If it corrupts you again, it's possible you might take on a new form entirely.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: That's exactly why I have to go... why I should be at the very front.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: ...! You mean...

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: Yes, I intend to lure it into my body.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: That's too risky. If things get out of hand, I might have to kill you. Do you understand how dangerous this is?

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: I understand. But if I do this, you'll have a clear and visible target.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: The Devorator will have a hard time passing up the chance to enter a body it knows how to control. You won't have to worry about any of your friends being taken over.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: You're not like me, Miss Clorinde. You're a just and powerful Marechaussee Hunter. This monster broke free due to my error. It's only right that I shoulder the responsibility for its destruction.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: This is... something that I have to do.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: Consider it a duel to restore my honor. My only request is that you give it your all.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: ...I understand.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Then, as a Champion Duelist, I hereby accept your request for a duel, and extend to you my most sincere regards.

dialogues.speaker: Florian
dialogues.text: ...Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: The battle is now upon us. Let the Devorator once again tremble under the blade of the Marechaussee Hunters.

talks.objective: Enter the church in the capital

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: And so, the monsters were eradicated, and the sorcerer was defeated.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Peace soon returned to the capital. Those in the court manipulated by the sorcerer also recognized the errors of their ways...

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Some remembered the names of the heroes who saved their kingdom, but others simply continued their lives none the wiser.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Such is the story of the Marechaussee Hunters. They pursue the phantoms in the darkness and exterminate all who pose a threat...

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: They will always protect the city and those within it, even should all memory of their accomplishments be forgotten by the very people they serve.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Whew... I'm assuming we've finally reached the end of the script?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Yes. You've reached one of the better endings.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: It's a pretty solid story overall. I thought it was just an ordinary adventure at first, but the further we got into it, the more impressed I became with the production and the plot.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: That final battle especially! All the effects were super realistic.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Right, yeah, hehe... totally.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Ah... That's a really good point. I never expected the weapons we picked up from that vault would have that kind of effect.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Yeah, mine nearly scared the daylights out of me when it started glowing! I took a good look at it after we got out, but I don't think it ever lit up again.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Oh, we should probably give these props back, right? I'll just leave mine here.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Did you have a good time?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Of course. Let me know if another script like this comes around!

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Sure, no problem.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Then, I'll head back for now. I think I need some time to fully digest everything that just happened.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Once Mr. Florian is awake, please pass on my regards to him. He must be extremely exhausted, to have passed out cold like that.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: You're right. He's had a lot to deal with.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Well, see you all some other time! Toodle-oo!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: ...Okay, so, can I ask now?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I think it should be fine, yeah.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: What in the world was going on back there?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: ...Ah, so you saw through all of that?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Ahahaha... That time in the cave when you told us to close our eyes... It'd be weirder if we didn't notice anything.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I was dying of curiosity the entire time! I mean, you did a pretty bang-up job of pretending nothing had gone wrong. Furina actually looked like she thought all of it was planned...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Guess none of us wanted to be the one to break the illusion.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What are you all talking about?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Wait, don't tell me you never...! Ah, this is all my fault. It's not too late to cover your ears! Here, partner, I'll do it for you!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Um... Bit late for that, don't you think?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... You're saying... Everything that happened back there wasn't actually part of the script?

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: It's probably more accurate to say this was never a real scripted story to begin with.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whaaat!?

response.speaker: Florian
response.text: ...So loud... My head...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, you! Get up right now and explain yourself!

response.speaker: Florian
response.text: Ahhhhh! No shaking, please! My head...!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Florian explains the truth to everyone...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: D—Did Paimon just hear that right? You guys made up that whole last part on the spot?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's not nice to lie to people, but.... Paimon's gotta admit, that was a really good story, Florian. Oh, and nice improvisation, Clorinde!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Yeah! It was like watching a magician improvise a spectacular magic trick after forgetting an important prop.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If Paimon knew something was wrong with that vault, she would've floated straight in the opposite direction!

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Everything was under control.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: As if you've ever described a situation as being "out of control." I'm pretty sure any situation you consider to be easy to handle would scare a reasonable person half to death!

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Guess I'm just used to it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... You must run into a lot of unexpected situations, then... That explains why you're so good at coming up with things on the spot...

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: As for you, Florian...

response.speaker: Florian
response.text: ...I know there's no excuse for what I did. I'll turn myself in to the Gardes at once, confess my crimes, and accept any punishment that comes my way.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: I would say you've already suffered more than enough.

response.speaker: Florian
response.text: ...What?

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: You may have been blinded by fame and fortune in the beginning, but your actions during the final battle had proven you to be a true Marechaussee Hunter.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: You'll be far more use to the city above ground than below. Your job as a Hunter is more important.

response.speaker: Florian
response.text: But...

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Of course, you'll still need to take the keys and pay a personal visit to the two Hunters you wronged. Prepare to accept any terms they give you as well.

response.speaker: Florian
response.text: ...Yes, of course.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: As far as I'm concerned, though... Your showing in the duel was enough to prove your honor.

response.speaker: Florian
response.text: ...! Then, I'll do exactly as you said. I... I'll go return those two keys right now.

response.speaker: Florian
response.text: Thank you so much, everyone. I'll do my best to prove myself worthy of the second chance you've given me. I swear this on my name and honor as a Marechaussee Hunter.

response.speaker: Florian
response.text: Until we meet again, everyone.

choices.text: I was just playing along too...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Wait, don't tell me Paimon never...! Ah, this is all my fault. It's not too late to cover your ears! Here, Paimon, I'll do it for you!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Speaking of Marechaussee Hunters... What should we do about the "treasure" in that cave?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Leave it be.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you sure? We could show it to people, make it so that the Hunters are remembered... Don't you want that?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: No. Every name on that tablet made the same choice. All Hunters know what the path entails.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I am no exception... My identity as a Marechaussee Hunter is not something I need people to remember. I wish only to be recognized as a Champion Duelist, nothing more.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: That's certainly very different from the path of a magician. Still, I admire your decision.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, Paimon just remembered something. If there were no special effects involved, why did our weapons begin to glow during the battle?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: That's because the Marechaussee Hunters of ages past would often imbue their weapons with special enchantments to suppress the monsters. Whenever a monster was nearby, their weapons would start to glow.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Ooh! So that's why they had an effect on that guy near the end. I really thought the summons were doing all the work.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Well, I'm sure the summons were a part of it, too.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Oh? How so?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: This particular Devorator probably hailed from the same era as the Hunters we saw in the room.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: The names you recited all belonged to the bravest Hunters. Countless monsters fell to their blades. That's likely why the Devorator visibly reacted when you said them out loud.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So the names held the power all along...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Navia, everything you said during your "summon"...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Huh? Ah—hahaha! I um, I meant what I said. I mean, it was true to my character! So, yeah, I'm glad you heard it, just don't make me repeat myself. It's embarrassing!

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I really appreciated those words.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Alright, alright. Don't get all sentimental on me.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Uhh... Anyway, let's not talk about that anymore! I'm going to go on ahead. Don't fall too far behind, now!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah... She ran off.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I should probably head back as well. This story was truly incredible. I might have to spend the whole night telling my siblings all about it!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you later.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Mhm, Goodbye!

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}... Should your name and deeds be forgotten, what do you think the significance of your journey will be?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I suppose the significance would be the journey itself and the world we helped create. There's still value in the time I shared with everyone here, in the things we were able to accomplish, even if no one remembers them.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: A great answer. I'll remember it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What would your answer be, Clorinde?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Me? Hah...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: "The Marechaussee Hunter says nothing in response to that question."

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: "Perhaps her answer lies in her silence, an unspoken vow left to echo through the night. The path she walks needs no explanation."

talks.objective: Leave the church in the capital

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You exit the basement shortly after Florian...
